subject: biology

hotspots.label: Parent alleles combine
hotspots.positionHint: Centered directly between the two father allele beads on the top edge (local coords roughly (0, 2.85, 0.12)) — the point that visibly touches both father beads (at x -0.15 and x 0.15) and reads as the row where alleles are supplied, with the mother's bead pair visible just below-left down the grid's side edge.
hotspots.description: Each parent contributes one allele per gene. The father's two alleles line up along the top edge of the grid; the mother's two line up down the left edge. Where a row and column meet, their alleles combine to form an offspring's genotype.

hotspots.label: Punnett square grid
hotspots.positionHint: Dead center of the vertical grid slab, local coords roughly (0, 1.85, 0.08) — front face, midpoint of the four cells and their dividers.
hotspots.description: The 2x2 grid itself: four cells, each showing the genotype produced by one father-allele/mother-allele combination. It's the tool geneticists use to predict all possible offspring outcomes from a single cross.

hotspots.label: Predicted genotype ratios
hotspots.positionHint: Left cluster on the pedestal shelf below the grid, local coords roughly (-0.45, 0.21, 0.4) — center of the three-tower stack group, with the y-coordinate resting on the actual disk geometry (towers rise from base y=0.15 up to roughly y=0.27 for the tallest 2-disk tower).
hotspots.description: Counting the four grid cells gives the expected genotype ratio (e.g. 1 homozygous-dominant : 2 heterozygous : 1 homozygous-recessive for a classic monohybrid cross). Shown as a small cluster of stacked disk-towers whose heights encode the ratio.

hotspots.label: Predicted phenotype ratios
hotspots.positionHint: Right cluster on the pedestal shelf below the grid, local coords roughly (0.45, 0.25, 0.4) — center of the two-tower stack group, with the y-coordinate resting on the actual disk geometry (towers rise from base y=0.15 up to roughly y=0.33 for the tallest 3-disk tower).
hotspots.description: Genotypes translate to observable traits. Dominant and recessive genotypes that share the same visible trait are grouped, giving the phenotype ratio (e.g. 3 dominant-trait : 1 recessive-trait). Shown as a second, smaller disk-tower cluster beside the genotype stacks.

visualStyleNotes: Reads as a single calm "specimen object" in the Anatomy Atelier language, not a UI diagram: a vertical punnett-square slab floating above the same warm matte pedestal dome seen in desktop-overview.png/desktop-interaction.png, with two small satellite clusters resting on a shelf in front of the pedestal. No literal grid-app or spreadsheet look. Deviates from Atelier's default in one deliberate way: autoRotateDefault is false, because the grid carries letters/text that must stay legible and unmirrored — the object opens in a fixed 3/4-front view instead of spinning, and the learner opts into rotation manually (a "physically meaningful control," per spec section 12, not a default show-off spin). Hotspot dots use the same small flat-colored circular markers as the reference, sized ~0.05 units, offset 0.02 units in front of surface geometry to avoid z-fighting. Palette pulls the Biology identity from spec section 12: warm paper/off-white base (~#F5EFE6), coral accent (~#E0785B) for dominant traits, leaf green (~#6B8F71) for recessive traits, graphite/ink (~#3A342C) for engraved text and divider lines — used as thin accent rings, never as flat saturated fills, so the piece stays in the calm/scientific register rather than reading as a toy.
materialNotes: Matte ceramic/porcelain-paper shader throughout (MeshStandardMaterial-equivalent: roughness ~0.6-0.7, metalness 0, no emissive, no bloom/glow). Punnett grid slab: warm paper/off-white (~#F5EFE6), subtle micro-roughness, zero specularity spike — eggshell ceramic, not plastic. Divider lines: shallow engraved grooves in graphite/ink (~#3A342C) with soft AO, not applied decals. Parent and offspring allele beads: same ceramic material as the slab body, with a single engraved humanist-sans letter per bead; letter case (upper/lower) always carries the dominant/recessive distinction, never color alone. Genotype ratio disk stacks: same warm-paper ceramic, with an engraved monospace-style ratio plaque beneath the cluster. Phenotype ratio disk stacks: same ceramic base with a thin rim accent ring in coral (~#E0785B, dominant) or leaf green (~#6B8F71, recessive) — the only place flat color-coding appears, and always paired with the plaque numerals, never color alone. Lighting: soft 3-point warm studio setup matching the Atelier reference renders, gentle contact AO under every bead and disk stack, no rim glow, no colored lights. Background: warm off-white with a very subtle radial vignette.
assetBrief:
OBJECT: "The Inheritance Table" — a procedural Three.js composition (primitives only: rounded boxes, capsules, cylinders/disks, thin plane dividers — no sculpted/organic geometry, no GLB needed). Build entirely from parametric primitives so genotype/ratio values can be swapped at runtime for different cross scenarios (e.g. monohybrid vs. test cross) without re-authoring geometry.

COMPOSITION (single centered object on the standard Atelier pedestal dome, local origin = top-center of pedestal, +y up, +z toward camera):

1. Pedestal: reuse the existing warm matte stone/plaster dome asset/material used for other Biology components (same silhouette as the heart/brain reference renders) — do not create a new pedestal style.

2. Punnett grid slab: a vertical rounded-corner slab, x: -0.85 to 0.85, y: 1.05 to 2.65 (1.6 tall x 1.7 wide), 0.06 thick, front face at z=0.03. Matte warm-paper/porcelain material (#F5EFE6-ish, subtle micro-roughness, zero specularity spike — think eggshell ceramic, not plastic). Two thin engraved graphite divider lines (one vertical, one horizontal) split the face into 4 equal cells, each ~0.85 wide x 0.8 tall. Divider lines are shallow grooves with soft AO, not applied decals.

3. Father allele pair (top, outside grid): two capsule "beads," each ~0.12 radius x 0.22 long, standing upright, centered at (-0.15, 2.85, 0.1) and (0.15, 2.85, 0.1) — spaced to align with the grid's two columns. Same ceramic material as the slab, with a single engraved serif letter per bead (e.g. "B" and "b" — uppercase for dominant, lowercase for recessive). Letter engraving carries the dominant/recessive distinction; do not rely on color alone.

4. Mother allele pair (left, outside grid): same bead geometry rotated 90°, centered at (-1.1, 2.0, 0.1) and (-1.1, 1.7, 0.1), aligned with the grid's two rows.

5. Offspring beads (inset in each of the 4 cells): smaller paired beads (~0.08 radius) sitting just in front of the cell face (z=0.09) at cell centers (-0.43, 2.25), (0.43, 2.25), (-0.43, 1.45), (0.43, 1.45) — each pair shows the combined genotype for that cell (e.g. "Bb", "BB", "bb"), letters engraved as in step 3.

6. Genotype ratio stacks (left shelf cluster): three disk-towers (flat cylinder "coins," ~0.22 radius, ~0.06 thick per disk, stacked) at x = -0.75, -0.45, -0.15, base y = 0.15, on the pedestal's front shelf, z ~0.3-0.5. Tower heights encode the ratio (e.g. 1:2:1 → 1, 2, 1 disks; the tallest 2-disk tower tops out around y=0.27). A small engraved plaque beneath the cluster carries the ratio in monospace-style numerals per spec section 12 (e.g. "1 : 2 : 1").

7. Phenotype ratio stacks (right shelf cluster): two disk-towers at x = 0.25, 0.65, same base y and disk size as step 6, heights encoding e.g. 3:1 (the tallest 3-disk tower tops out around y=0.33). Disks get a thin coral or leaf-green accent ring on their rim (dominant vs. recessive trait) — the only place flat color-coding appears, and always paired with the plaque numerals, never color alone.

MATERIALS & LIGHTING: matte ceramic/ceramic-paper shader throughout (roughness ~0.6-0.7, no metalness, no emissive, no bloom/glow of any kind — spec section 12 explicitly forbids glow/gradient-heavy visuals). Soft 3-point warm studio lighting matching the Atelier reference renders, gentle contact AO under every bead and disk stack, warm-off-white background with a very subtle radial vignette (match desktop-overview.png).

TYPOGRAPHY ON-MODEL: engraved/embossed letters on beads use a humanist sans (matches spec's UI typeface direction), ratio plaques use a monospace-style face (matches spec's "monospace for formulas/data" rule) — never mix the two within one label.

CAMERA: default position (0, 1.9, 4.6), target (0, 1.55, 0.05), standard ~35-40° vertical FOV perspective — frames the full grid, both parent bead-pairs, and both shelf clusters with even margin, matching the large-centered-object framing in desktop-overview.png.

INTERACTION NOTES FOR PIPELINE: auto-rotate defaults off (see visualStyleNotes) but must still be toggleable; isolate control should support isolating "grid only," "parents only," or "ratios only" via the layers list; no cross-section control (nothing to section — surface it as unavailable/disabled rather than omitted, consistent with other components' viewer chrome); auto-rotate and any idle animation must pause whenever a hotspot card is open.

DO NOT: use bright saturated/cartoon colors as primary fills; add glow, bloom, or emissive materials; give beads faces/eyes or any cartoon character treatment; render a literal DNA double-helix (that belongs to the separate DNA component, not this one); use photographic/PBR-noisy textures — keep everything flat matte ceramic; encode dominant/recessive using color alone (colorblind-unsafe) — letters and plaque numerals must always carry the meaning; make the pedestal glossy or reflective; crowd the composition with extra labels beyond the four hotspot-triggered structure cards.
